title: Tensor unit
statement: For a scheme $T$, a commutative ring $\Lambda$, and $E\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, both canonical unit constraints $E\kunotimes{\Lambda}\underline{\Lambda}\to E$ and $\underline{\Lambda}\kunotimes{\Lambda}E\to E$ are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal O=\underline{\Lambda}$ using [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], for any $\mathcal O$-module sheaf $F$ the sectionwise maps $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$ and $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$ have inverses $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ and $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. They commute with restriction and hence induce inverse sheaf maps after sheafification. For any complex $C$, tensor with $\mathcal O[0]$ has only the summand $C^n\otimes\mathcal O$ (respectively $\mathcal O\otimes C^n$) in degree $n$. These maps commute with the differential since $d(ax)=a d(x)$; the total-tensor sign is $1$ in the second order because the first factor has degree zero. Thus both total tensor complexes are canonically isomorphic to $C$.

proof.text: Choose $C$ representing $E$ and a K-flat quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ as specified by [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The right derived tensor is represented by $P\otimes\mathcal O[0]$. Its right unit map is the degreewise isomorphism of step 1 followed by $P\to C$. Localization inverts this quasi-isomorphism, so the right unit constraint is invertible.

source.place: K-flat definition and displayed K-flat-model construction; elementary calculation expanding lem-kun-tensor-unit, Proof paragraph.

proof.text: Step 1 applied to an acyclic complex $A$ gives $\mathcal O[0]\otimes A\cong A$, so $\mathcal O[0]$ is K-flat by [def-kun-derived-tensor]. For the left derived tensor choose its identity K-flat resolution; it is represented by $\mathcal O[0]\otimes C$. Its left unit map is precisely the degreewise isomorphism in step 1, hence is invertible after localization. This establishes the left constraint for arbitrary, including unbounded, $E$.
